newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia urges world action on Internet child porn.
newsitem.headline: Australia urges world action on Internet child porn.

text.p: Australia said on Wednesday it would push for concerted international action against paedophile rings using the Internet.

Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer said he would raise measures to stamp out international paedophile networks at next month's meeting of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).

"I will be pursuing in the OECD meeting the agony associated with the internationalisation of paedophilia and the initiative of the Belgium government to raise several of these matters in the OECD context," said Fischer.

Belgium has led European efforts to crack down on paedophile networks and child pornography, particularly through the Internet, after being rocked by a paedophile scandal involving the murders of five girls.

"We are examining the detail of the Belgium government proposals, but I have to say the Australian government is aware there is an internationalisation of paedophilia networks," Fischer told reporters.
The 28-nation OECD comprises the world's major developed nations, which have among the highest rates of computer usage.
